title: Choose the dashboard's visual world
question: Robot Telemetry redesign: status at a glance, barcode mapping beside Mission state. Keep the roll, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Swiss Grid Bulletin
options.thesis: Robot health set as a strict flush-left typographic grid where state is the headline and red means stop.
options.viewport: Top bar with link and frame age; a six-cell status row (Mission, Line, Obstacle, Terrain, Motion, Faults) with each state set large and flush-left; mapping panel docked right of Mission with four letter inputs and Send; speed chart and event log below on the same grid.
options.risk: Can turn cold and poster-like if the grid crowds out standard controls.

raised.raise: The 12-column grid is a real layout armature, shown as hairlines, not decoration.
Severity uses a fixed size ramp: an active fault grows its cell's rule, so it reads before any word.
Nothing disappears: cleared faults and refused mappings stay in the log struck through.
Each subsystem has fixed slots that never move, so the eye learns where everything lives.

options.label: MRT Line Map
options.lineage: Singapore MRT system map and station signage
options.thesis: Each subsystem is a coloured line, and the run's event record is drawn as a route of stations.
options.viewport: Header with link pills; six subsystem tiles each tagged with its line colour; mapping panel beside Mission; a horizontal route strip where barcodes, humps, obstacles and turns appear as stations with time and encoder position.
options.risk: Familiar local reference; the route strip is only approximate because there is no localisation.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Subsystems as board rows in fixed columns; mapping letters set in flap cells.
options.viewport: Dark board: one row per subsystem with state, value and fault columns; four flap cells for L R S U with Send; events as a departures list below.
options.case: Fuses well: subsystems map to rows and the four letters to flap cells; holds clarity but is less familiar to a bench team.
options.risk: Flip animation can lag a 500 ms stream and read as novelty.

options.label: Graphite Console
options.thesis: Hairline-seamed graphite panels; the Send mapping action stands alone so it is never hit by accident.
options.viewport: Persistent panels: status column left, mapping panel top right with isolated Send, chart and event log filling the rest.
options.case: Very clear working product; loses on identity since it looks like every dev tool.
options.risk: Close to the category default and dim on a bright lab bench.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: Mapping letters drawn cell by cell.
options.case: Near-duplicate of the roll with weaker clarity.
options.kept: A visible grid that is the real layout armature.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Magnitude as dot size on a navy chart.
options.case: Team does not identify with it and states become harder to read.
options.kept: A fixed size ramp for severity.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.kept: A finite roster with fixed slots per member.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light card-grid telemetry dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Header pills, a grid of status cards with a mapping card first, chart and log below.
canonCard.risk: Close to today's dashboard; little to tell it apart.
